clinician.final_diagnosis: 4 mm acute left lateral medullary infarct of the left posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) vascular territory
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old patient with multiple vascular risk factors presented with left-sided paresthesias, hemiparesis, ataxic gait, and craniofacial pain. Neurological examination revealed left Horner’s syndrome, ipsilateral facial numbness, contralateral loss of temperature sensation, and left-sided hemiparesis consistent with lateral medullary syndrome. Brain MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging documented a 4 mm acute infarct in the left lateral medulla in the left PICA vascular territory. Carotid ultrasound and CT angiography showed moderate right internal carotid artery stenosis but no large vessel intracranial stenosis. The patient received anticoagulation and symptomatic treatment with gradual neurological improvement and was discharged with rehabilitation recommendations.
